# PSY Lokalpsykiatri Almen (Esbjerg)

PSY Lokalpsykiatri Almen (Esbjerg) is a psychiatric outpatient unit reported on in the Danish ADHD quality database (ADHD_2024.pdf), where it appears as a data point in two separate quality indicators tracking care for adult ADHD patients. The unit's most notable result is a 14% fulfillment rate on Indicator 10, far below the national quality target of 90% [^src1].

Indicator 10 measures the share of adult treatment courses in which a patient's social support needs were assessed within 120 days of starting treatment — the first time this indicator has been reported in the database [^src1]. Nationally, fulfillment stood at only 37%, with regional results ranging from 14% to 52%, meaning Esbjerg's local unit performed at the very bottom of that national range [^src1]. For PSY Lokalpsykiatri Almen (Esbjerg), the raw figures behind the 14% result were 10 fulfilled cases out of 70 treatment courses, with a confidence interval of 7–25% [^src1]. The steering group behind the database has discussed possible causes for such low fulfillment nationwide, pointing to registration practices and data quality issues at child and adolescent psychiatric outpatient clinics and private hospitals, and has committed to working on improving registration practices going forward [^src1].

The unit also appears in the database's results for Indicator 11, which measures the share of adult treatment courses where the patient was in ADHD medication treatment within 120 days of starting a care pathway — also reported for adults for the first time in 2024, following the database's expansion that year [^src2]. Here, PSY Lokalpsykiatri Almen (Esbjerg) performed much better, with 62 out of 70 cases fulfilled, a rate of 89% (confidence interval 79–95%) [^src2]. This places the unit close to the national quality target and stands in contrast to its low score on Indicator 10, illustrating how performance can vary sharply between different quality measures at the same clinical unit. Nationally, Indicator 11 results also showed wide regional variation — from Region Nordjylland at 85% to Region Hovedstaden at 37% — which the database attributes largely to differences in registration practices rather than genuine differences in clinical care [^src2].
